key_insight: DSWorld learns a data-science world model that predicts workflow state transitions before execution, reducing costly trial-and-error in autonomous agents.
engineering_relevance: It can speed up agent training and search-based inference for data science workflows while preserving competitive performance.
method: Builds structured workflow states from the current data science environment and candidate operations.
Uses cost-aware routing to choose between real execution, lightweight execution, and an LLM-based simulator for expensive operations.
Trains with an 8K transition trajectory dataset and Reflective World Model Optimization to improve error-sensitive transition prediction.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports about 14× faster RL-based agent training, 3–6× faster search-based inference, and 35.6% better transition prediction than the strongest LLM baseline.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of state construction and simulator routing, and the approach may need careful validation when generalizing to new data science tools or workflows.
paper_title: DSWorld: A Data Science World Model for Efficient Autonomous Agents
